wholeHouse.internalNote: Estimated illustrative finish prices, CSS textures only (no photos) — not the real quote. Two things worth knowing: 'White Render' and 'Cream Render' here (£45/m²) are close to but different from the real Alabaster render swatch already priced at £50/m² in the cladding catalogue above, and 'Brick Slips' here (£85/m² of wall area) is a different product and unit than 'Brick Slip' in the Roofline & Cladding tab (£110 per linear metre of trim). Use the real cladding/roof/trim visualizer for a sourced quote.

conservatories.note: Broad guide ranges to help compare styles. A conservatory is priced on size, glazing, groundworks and access.

styles.name: Edwardian
styles.description: Clean rectangular footprint maximising usable floor space. Timeless flat-fronted elevation with strong symmetry.

styles.name: Victorian
styles.description: Iconic faceted bay front adding character and wide-angle views. The classic UK conservatory silhouette.
cons: More complex roof, higher cost than a simple rectangle

styles.name: Lean-to
styles.description: Simple single-pitch roof leaning against the house. Lowest height, ideal for restricted spaces and contemporary bungalows.

styles.name: Gable
styles.description: High gable front with a full-height triangular frame. Cathedral-like feel, with the most light and volume of the simpler styles.
cons: Needs sufficient wall height/space to suit the proportions

styles.name: P-shaped
styles.description: Combines a lean-to and Victorian bay to wrap around a corner. Creates two distinct living zones in one structure.

styles.name: T-shaped
styles.description: A central projection creates a symmetrical T shape, with a dramatic central avenue and wings either side.

styles.name: Orangery
styles.description: Brick or stone pillars with a flat perimeter roof and a central roof lantern. A luxury solid-roof hybrid between an extension and a conservatory.
pros: Better year-round insulation than an all-glass roof
cons: Less roof glazing than a full glass-roof style

styles.name: Garden Room
styles.description: Fully tiled, lightweight roof with bi-fold doors across the front. A true year-round room that feels like a proper extension.
pros: Feels like a real room, not a conservatory
cons: Least roof glazing/natural light of the 8 styles

conservatories.internalNote: ESTIMATED placeholder price ranges — unlike cladding/roof/trim above, these are NOT sourced from any real production data. Replace with real supplier/installer pricing whenever you have it.

windowsDoors.note: Style and colour preview. Windows and doors are quoted separately, on frame size and glazing spec.

windowStyles.name: Casement
windowStyles.description: Side-hinged opening pane with a classic cross-bar divide. The most common UK window style.

windowStyles.name: Flush
windowStyles.description: Flat, flush-fitting sash that sits within the frame for a clean, modern, low-profile look.

windowStyles.name: Sliding Sash
windowStyles.description: Two vertically sliding panels in a traditional box frame — period character with modern double glazing.

windowStyles.name: Bay
windowStyles.description: Angled multi-pane projection that adds floor space and lets in light from three directions.

doorStyles.name: Composite Door
doorStyles.description: Solid, high-security composite panel door — durable, low-maintenance, and available in any colour.

doorStyles.name: Bifold
doorStyles.description: Folding panels that stack to one side, opening the full width onto a garden or patio.

windowsDoors.internalNote: Style and colour preview only — window/door pricing depends on frame size, glazing spec, and installation, so no price range is shown here. Use the cladding/roof/trim visualizer above for a real priced quote.

fsgc.note: Guide per-metre prices for comparing profiles. Your estimate uses our standard sourced specification.
fsgc.internalNote: ESTIMATED per-metre guide prices for style comparison only — these are NOT the same numbers as the real, sourced trim rates used in the quote engine above (fascia £35/m + £12/m labour, soffit £30/m + £12/m labour, guttering £40/m + £15/m labour, from quote_generator.py), and cladding here is priced per linear metre for illustration whereas the real cladding catalogue is priced per m² of wall area. Don't treat these as a real quote — use the visualizer above for that.

glazing.note: Guide prices for supply and fitting, per window and per door, including access and VAT.
glazing.internalNote: Door rates are real. Window bands are still invented and running at roughly half of trade. See notes/glazing-rates-from-the-trade.md.
glazing.source: Prices are what jobs settle at, from 24 years selling for a national installer, inclusive of VAT and stored net. The base is close to the keener of the two installers who buy leads here; Anglian settles about 1.6x higher on doors and 2x on a 3 m bifold, which is what the estimate range spans. Checked 2026-08-06 against Anglian list prices less the 40% discount routinely available. Not a supplier rate card. Openers are not yet modelled and a window with none is dearer here than it should be — see notes/glazing-rates-from-the-trade.md.

windowBands.label: Standard
windowBands.example: 1200 x 1200 — most bedroom and lounge windows

windowBands.label: Extra large
windowBands.example: Picture windows and wide mullioned units

glazing.vatNote: Replacement windows and doors in an existing dwelling are standard-rated. The energy-saving materials relief does not cover them.
glazing.openerNote: Cost of one opening light, net, on top of the band price. The bands assume one opener, which is the common case. Derived from a standard window quoted at £950 with none and £2,247 with two, less the 40% discount: £570 and £1,348 inclusive, so £389 inclusive per opener, £324 net. Flat rather than scaled by band, because an opening light is hardware and frame rather than glass — it costs much the same in a small window as a large one. One measured product; revisit when there are more.
